items.question: Why does DeepWalk's negative sampling objective make its hierarchical softmax updates faster to compute than the standard skip-gram objective?
items.false_premise: DeepWalk uses negative sampling and compares it against a standard skip-gram objective.
items.correction: DeepWalk uses hierarchical softmax, not negative sampling, to factor the conditional probabilities.
items.evidence_quote: Hierarchical Softmax factors out Pr( v3| Φ(v1)) and Pr(v5| Φ(v1)) over sequences of probability distributions corresponding to the paths starting at the root and ending at v3 and v5.

items.question: How does DeepWalk's use of a lock on shared parameters help it avoid the sparse-update problem in its multi-worker training?
items.false_premise: DeepWalk uses a lock on shared parameters during multi-worker training.
items.correction: DeepWalk explicitly says it does not acquire a lock when accessing shared parameters in ASGD.
items.evidence_quote: Given that our updates are sparse and we do not acquire a lock to access the model shared parameters, ASGD will achieve an optimal rate of convergence [36].

items.question: What evidence shows that DeepWalk's parallelization hurts predictive performance on BlogCatalog and Flickr once the number of workers reaches 8?
items.false_premise: DeepWalk's parallelization hurts predictive performance on BlogCatalog and Flickr at 8 workers.
items.correction: The passage says parallelization yields consistent speedup and no loss of predictive performance relative to serial execution.
items.evidence_quote: It also shows that there is no loss of predictive performance relative to the running DeepW alkserially (Figure 4b).

items.question: Under which conditions does DeepWalk require knowledge of the entire graph for its streaming variant to work?
items.false_premise: DeepWalk's streaming variant requires knowledge of the entire graph.
items.correction: The streaming variant could be implemented without knowledge of the entire graph.
items.evidence_quote: One interesting variant of this method is a streaming approach, which could be implemented without knowledge of the entire graph.
